design_identity.palette: warm desert ochre, muted clay red, deep indigo, restrained antique gold
design_identity.texture: sun-baked earth, woven tent cloth, weathered stone; subtle and dignified
design_identity.lighting: clear dry-country light with warm directional highlights and natural shadow
design_identity.mood: inheritance, tension between siblings, divine promise carried through an unsettled household
design_identity.continuity: family-centered patriarchal world with restrained drama; visual tension may be present without caricaturing either brother

scene_rules.world: ancient Near East appropriate to Genesis, especially pastoral encampments, open field, wells, and the southern Canaan/Gerar environment
scene_rules.people: plausible ancient Near Eastern dress and material culture; no later Jewish or Christian costume conventions
scene_rules.architecture: tents, simple stone or mud-brick structures, wells and pastoral landscape where supported by the current aliyah
avoid: halos, crosses or later religious symbols
visual moral stereotyping of Jacob or Esau
locking any one aliyah-specific person, meal, birth scene, famine scene, or well scene into the parasha-wide profile

typographic_accent.rule: retain GLOBAL IMAGE MASTER hierarchy; use antique-gold rules and small clay-red accents sparingly
typographic_accent.parasha_identity: the palette and material atmosphere should unify all Toledot aliyot while the right-side narrative scene changes strictly with each current passage
